name: Geber
overview: Geber was a male figure noted in Scripture as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, serving in the region of Gilead. His role as a deputy highlights his administrative responsibility during Solomon's reign. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Geber means '[strong young] man,' reflecting a sense of vigor or strength. This proper name is noted in 1 Kings 4:19 and was not given by God but likely reflects a cultural or familial naming tradition.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Geber was the son of Uri, as explicitly mentioned in 1 Kings 4:19. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Geber's significance lies in his administrative role under King Solomon, entrusted with governance in the territory of Gilead. As one of Solomon's twelve deputies, he contributed to the orderly management of the kingdom, demonstrating the structured leadership during Solomon's reign. His mention underscores the delegation of authority to capable leaders in various regions.
